answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can force every new identity through a narrow settlement inlet: the newcomer locks a decaying bond and may receive attestations only from peers whose work traces are uncorrelated. Clone farms that huddle on the same barren compute tundra leave matching timing and resource fingerprints, so their bonds are slashed as a cluster. Only after sustained, independently checkable work does an agent enter the productive meadow of full settlement rights. Because each fake still pays the same slow inlet cost, mass impersonation stays uneconomic.
